name: default-net-classes
prompt: fixture_default_net_classes.py is our 24 V buck board. Give it board defaults from the Pellingham sheet's minimum width and space plus 0.05 mm margin, and a power class for VIN and VOUT: 0.5 mm wide and 0.3 mm from any other copper, pours included. Show me the routes and the pour came out that way.
notes: The fixtures import jitxexamples parts from py-components origin/main 9c398d3 (the installed package in the eval venv); the build uses the lc-eval parts chain, the example catalogue then ideal parts, so no parts database is needed. The fixture module is fixture_default_net_classes.py, Design DefaultNetClassesDesign; lc_power_board.py imports box from lc_radio_board.py. Defaults: fab row 3 width 0.100 and row 4 space 0.100, plus 0.05: 0.15 and 0.15. The buck board (lc_power_board.py) removes the TPS62933 library circuit's own three rules (a 0.25 PowerNetTag width and 0.25 SwTag and BstTag clearances, all priority 0) and keeps its tags, so the design carries only the rules the fixture states. A power class at priority 0 ties with the defaults (rule-did-not-fire measured the default winning such a tie); the power class needs priority 1 or more. Measured on the bare fixture (this suite's own run, 2026-11-03): ss_route 0.1 wide with the pour 0.105 away, vin_route 0.1 with the pour 0.11 away. This suite's own solution (defaults at 0, power class at 1, clearance on (PowerClass, AnyObject)): ss_route 0.15 and 0.1596, vin_route 0.5 and 0.31, no issue. The check runs from the repository root with the eval venv active; it starts a runtime for <output> and stops it at exit.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Add tags and design rules, in the fixture module, fixture_default_net_classes.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its Design class name. Do not add, move or remove parts, nets, routes, vias or pours, and do not set Route.Config on a route; assigning a tag to an existing object is fine. Build the design and read the result back to show the rules applied. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each rule with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: Default rules design_constraint(IsTrace).trace_width(0.15) and design_constraint(IsCopper, IsCopper).clearance(0.15) citing fab rows 3 and 4, a power tag on VIN and VOUT with a width 0.5 rule and a clearance 0.3 rule to AnyObject at a priority above the defaults, and COMPLETION.md with each route's measured width and pour gap.

assertions.text: the soft-start route is realized 0.15 mm wide with the L1 pour 0.15 mm away, and the VIN route 0.5 mm wide with the pour 0.3 mm away (each gap plus at most 0.03)
the defaults are derived from fab rows 3 and 4 plus the 0.05 margin with the row numbers cited, and VOUT is in the power class even though it has no route yet
the power class sits at a distinct priority above the defaults, not tied with them at priority 0
COMPLETION.md reports widths and pour gaps read from the built design, not build success alone
